methods.label: Use the two cut lengths
methods.explanation:
The parallel cuts create smaller equilateral triangles: corresponding angles in \(ADE\) and \(AFG\) are all \(60^\circ\). Thus each cut length also equals the lengths of the two sides from \(A\) to that cut.

Let
\[
x=DE=AD=AE,\qquad y=FG=AF=AG.
\]
The order of the points in the figure gives \(0<x<y<1\). Subtracting lengths along the sides gives
\[
DF=EG=y-x,\qquad FB=GC=1-y.
\]
We can now express all three perimeters using just \(x\) and \(y\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{ADE}&=3x,\\
P_{DFGE}&=x+y+2(y-x)=3y-x,\\
P_{FBCG}&=y+1+2(1-y)=3-y.
\end{aligned}
\]
Equating the first perimeter with each of the other two gives
\[
4x=3y,\qquad 3x+y=3.
\]
The first equation gives \(y=4x/3\). Substituting this into the second eliminates \(y\):
\[
3x+\frac{4x}{3}=3,
\qquad 13x=9.
\]
Therefore \(x=9/13\) and \(y=12/13\). These satisfy \(0<x<y<1\), and all three perimeters equal \(27/13\), so the lengths meet the original conditions. Hence
\[
DE+FG=\frac{9}{13}+\frac{12}{13}
=\boxed{\frac{21}{13}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
